facts.fact: Madhya Pradesh had 785 of India's 3,682 tigers in 2022, 21%, and 222 more than Karnataka, next with 563.
facts.measure: Tigers (All India Tiger Estimation)
facts.compare: India 3,682; Karnataka 563; Uttarakhand 560; Madhya Pradesh has 9.4% of India's area
facts.stays_true: The Government calls the Estimation quadrennial (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022); the next cycle's figures are not on the drive and would be a new count. Numbers for 2022 stay what they are; 'latest' would change when the next cycle is published. No newer Lok Sabha answer on the drive carries state tiger counts (ls_find tiger). Cross-check: the same state figures are in the NTCA/WII 'Status of Tigers 2022' report (saved by the land collector as evergreen/land_tigers_2022: Madhya Pradesh 785 with standard error 58, Karnataka 563 (35), Uttarakhand 560 (24), Maharashtra 444 (43), India 3,682 (243)).
facts.lead: 222 tigers, 39% over Karnataka; 6.0 points of India's total
facts.size_effect: Madhya Pradesh has 9.4% of the area but 21.3% of the tigers: 2.5 tigers per 1,000 sq km (India 1.1).
facts.caution: AITE figures are estimates for tiger-bearing landscapes, not a count of every tiger; the answer calls them 'tiger numbers'. Karnataka (563) and Uttarakhand (560) are close to each other: do not rank them against each other. The NTCA report gives standard errors (Madhya Pradesh plus or minus 58; India plus or minus 243): say 'estimated'.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 953, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 02.12.2024: "Decreasing Tiger Population"
facts.as_on: All India Tiger Estimation 2022; answer dated 2 December 2024

facts.fact: In the 2025 revision West Bengal's coastline went from 157.5 km to 721.02 km, now longer than Kerala's 600.15 km.
facts.measure: Length of coastline, old and revised
facts.compare: old 157.5 km (4.6 times smaller); Kerala 569.7 km old and 600.15 km revised; Odisha 574.71 km
facts.source: Ministry of Earth Sciences, Parliament answer 'Coastline of the Country', PIB 4 Dec 2025 (old and revised side by side); Survey of India note
facts.as_on: Revised length promulgated 29 April 2025; Parliament answer 4 December 2025
facts.stays_true: Fixed until the next 10-year review (about 2035).
facts.lead: Revised: 120.87 km (20%) over Kerala; old: Kerala was ahead by 412.2 km
facts.size_effect: Not a size effect: a within-state change between two measurements.
facts.caution: The Survey of India gives one general reason for all states (map scale and calculation method, offshore islands added); it does not explain West Bengal's change separately, so do not suggest a cause, and do not say the coast 'grew'.

facts.fact: Manipur has 204,508 women handloom weavers, more than West Bengal's 175,751, with 3% of West Bengal's people.
facts.measure: Women handloom weavers
facts.compare: West Bengal 175,751; Tamil Nadu 93,448; India 1,914,499; Manipur 10.7% of India's women weavers
facts.source: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles, Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20, Annexure II Tables 1-2 (handlooms.nic.in/assets/img/Statistics/3736.pdf)
facts.stays_true: A census of 2019-20; changes with the Fifth Handloom Census.
facts.lead: 28,757 ahead (16% more) than West Bengal, third; Assam is first with 1,031,717. In 2009-10 (adult weavers) Manipur 199,111 led West Bengal 148,117
facts.size_effect: Manipur is 0.23% of India's people, so its 10.7% share is 46x its population share.
facts.caution: Second-place claim for Manipur is true on both censuses behind Assam. West Bengal's population is the 1 March 2020 projection.

facts.fact: Gujarat has the most universities of any state, 107, against Uttar Pradesh's 103, with under a third of its people (AISHE 2023-24).
facts.measure: Universities registered in AISHE (all types)
facts.compare: Uttar Pradesh 103.0; Rajasthan 93. Gujarat has 73.2 million people against Uttar Pradesh's 240.5 (projected, 1 Mar 2025): 30% as many.
facts.source: Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education: All India Survey on Higher Education 2023-24, Table 1 (page T-1)
facts.stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'.
facts.lead: 4 universities (3.9%) in 2023-24; in AISHE 2022-23 it was 102 against 94 (8.5%)
facts.size_effect: Per million people Gujarat has 1.46 universities, Uttar Pradesh 0.43, India 0.91.
facts.caution: The lead over Uttar Pradesh in 2023-24 is 3.9%: it clears the 3% rule narrowly and held in both editions. 65 of Gujarat's 107 are state private universities. Do not use with built-13 in one video.

facts.fact: Uttarakhand had 560 of India's 3,682 tigers in 2022, 15%, on 1.6% of India's land.
facts.measure: Tigers (All India Tiger Estimation)
facts.compare: India 3,682; Uttarakhand has 1.63% of India's geographical area and 0.84% of projected population (1 March 2026); 10.5 tigers per 1,000 sq km against India's 1.1
facts.stays_true: The Government calls the Estimation quadrennial (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022); the next cycle's figures are not on the drive and would be a new count. Numbers for 2022 stay what they are; 'latest' would change when the next cycle is published. No newer Lok Sabha answer on the drive carries state tiger counts (ls_find tiger). Cross-check: the same state figures are in the NTCA/WII 'Status of Tigers 2022' report (saved by the land collector as evergreen/land_tigers_2022: Madhya Pradesh 785 with standard error 58, Karnataka 563 (35), Uttarakhand 560 (24), Maharashtra 444 (43), India 3,682 (243)).
facts.lead: Third in the state list (Madhya Pradesh 785, Karnataka 563, Uttarakhand 560): no rank claimed
facts.size_effect: Share of tigers (15.2%) is 9.3 times its share of land; a rate, not a size effect.
facts.caution: Do not say 'third': Karnataka is only 3 ahead. The area share uses geographical area printed in the ISFR 2023 table in Lok Sabha Q 304 (2 Feb 2026).
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 953, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 02.12.2024: "Decreasing Tiger Population"
facts.as_on: All India Tiger Estimation 2022; answer dated 2 December 2024
facts.why: the same tiger estimate, from a Lok Sabha answer

facts.fact: Mizoram was 52.1% urban in Census 2011, more than Tamil Nadu (48.4%) or Maharashtra (45.2%); only Goa (62.2%) was higher among States.
facts.measure: Urban population as a share of total population
facts.compare: India 31.1%; Tamil Nadu 48.4%, Kerala 47.7%, Maharashtra 45.2%; only Goa (62.2%) is higher among States
facts.source: Census of India 2011, Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India, Table A-01 (Number of villages, towns, households, population and area), read 13 Oct 2026
facts.stays_true: Census 2011 share; next census results expected from 2027.
facts.lead: Second among States after Goa; 52.11% against Tamil Nadu 48.40% (third), 3.7 points ahead. Census 2001 (checked): Mizoram 49.63%, Goa 49.76%, Tamil Nadu 44.04%, Maharashtra 42.43%, Kerala 25.96%
facts.size_effect: A share, and Mizoram is small (10.97 lakh people), so it is the rate, not the size, that stands out.
facts.caution: Kerala's urban share was 26.0% in Census 2001 and 47.7% in 2011 (more towns counted), so avoid a 'Kerala' comparison beyond 2011. Do not say Mizoram is the second most urban 'place': Delhi, Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu and Puducherry (Union Territories) are higher. Say 'second among States'.

facts.fact: Gujarat has 22% of India's wetland area, 3.5 million hectares, on 6% of the land (Atlas 2021).
facts.measure: Wetland area, National Wetland Atlas 2021
facts.compare: India 15,981,516 ha; next state Maharashtra 1,152,625 ha (3.0 times smaller); Gujarat has 6.0% of India's geographical area
facts.stays_true: Wetland areas come from the National Wetland Atlas, which has had two editions (2011: 15.26 million ha, 2021: 15.98 million ha, both in Lok Sabha Q 3809 of 24 Mar 2025); Gujarat was first in both. A third Atlas is not announced in the answer. The Atlas answer of 20 July 2026 is the newest on the drive (ls_find wetland).
facts.lead: 3.0 times Maharashtra; 14.7 points of India's total
facts.size_effect: Share of wetland (21.9%) is 3.7 times its share of land.
facts.caution: The Atlas maps every wetland of 2.25 ha or more, including the Rann, coastal mudflats, salt pans, tanks and reservoirs: say 'wetland' as the Atlas does, not 'lakes' or 'Ramsar sites'.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 208, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 20.07.2026: "Protection and Preservation of Wetlands in Assam"
facts.as_on: National Wetland Atlas 2021 (SAC, ISRO); answer dated 20 July 2026

facts.fact: Karnataka's 231 dams hold 30.8 billion cubic metres, two-thirds of the 46.8 held by Maharashtra's 2,696 (April 2025).
facts.measure: Gross storage capacity of specified dams
facts.compare: Maharashtra 46.789 BCM in 2,696 dams. Average per dam: Karnataka 133 million cubic metres, Maharashtra 17, India 50.
facts.source: National Dam Safety Authority, Ministry of Jal Shakti: National Register of Specified Dams, April 2025 (summary table, page iv)
facts.stays_true: Counts change only when dams are completed or added to the register; the register is re-issued every few years (2023, then April 2025). The April 2025 figures stay true as dated. Next edition date not announced.
facts.lead: Not a rank claim
facts.size_effect: Karnataka has 8.6% of Maharashtra's dam count but 65.8% of its gross storage; the contrast is in dam size, not state size (areas 191,791 and 307,713 sq km).
facts.caution: Counts 'specified dams' under the Dam Safety Act 2021 (above 15 m, or 10-15 m with size conditions), compiled from state dam safety organisations; many are small tanks and earthen dams, not big-river dams. Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu have no entry. The 2023 register (6,138 completed dams) could not be fetched from the publisher, so the lead is checked against the 2025 edition only. Gross storage is design capacity of the reservoir, not water in it on any day. Do not use with built-01/02 in one video (same table).

facts.fact: 18% of Gujarat's land is mapped as wetland, the most of any State; India's share is 5% (Atlas 2021).
facts.measure: Wetland area as a share of geographical area
facts.compare: India 4.9%; next state West Bengal 12.7%; Gujarat 3,499,429 ha of 19,624,400 ha
facts.stays_true: Wetland areas come from the National Wetland Atlas, which has had two editions (2011: 15.26 million ha, 2021: 15.98 million ha, both in Lok Sabha Q 3809 of 24 Mar 2025); Gujarat was first in both. A third Atlas is not announced in the answer. The Atlas answer of 20 July 2026 is the newest on the drive (ls_find wetland). The area base is the ISFR 2023 geographical area printed in Lok Sabha Q 304.
facts.lead: 5.1 points (40%) over West Bengal
facts.size_effect: A share of the state's own land.
facts.caution: Union Territories are left out of 'any State': Lakshadweep's lagoons exceed its tiny land (79,716 ha of wetland against 3,200 ha of land), the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are 17.4% (just below Gujarat) and Puducherry is 11%. Do not use together with the Gujarat wetland-share video.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 208, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 20.07.2026: "Protection and Preservation of Wetlands in Assam"
facts.as_on: National Wetland Atlas 2021 (SAC, ISRO); answer dated 20 July 2026

facts.fact: Kerala's forest cover grew 20% from 2013 to 2023, 3,675 square kilometres, the fastest of any State; India's grew 2.4%.
facts.measure: Change in forest cover 2013 to 2023
facts.compare: Kerala 18,384 to 22,059 sq km; India 2.38%; next state Andhra Pradesh 15.5%
facts.stays_true: Two fixed editions (ISFR 2013, ISFR 2023). The next State of Forest Report (ISFR 2025, expected about end-2026) will give a new 'ten years' pair and could change the order; the 2013-to-2023 statement stays true as written. Newest answer on the drive with the pair is Q 3461 (11 Aug 2025).
facts.lead: 4.5 points (29%) over Andhra Pradesh
facts.size_effect: A percentage change of its own 2013 cover.
facts.caution: Ladakh (+55%) and Chandigarh (+45%) are Union Territories with tiny or re-drawn bases: say 'any State'. The RBI Handbook notes some years are 'without normalisation'; the 2013 and 2023 figures are both 'without normalisation factor' but remain not strictly comparable with other years. Includes plantations and tree-covered holdings.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 3461, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 11.08.2025: "Tiger Reserve in Tamil Nadu"
facts.as_on: ISFR 2013 and ISFR 2023; answer dated 11 August 2025

facts.fact: Andhra Pradesh added 4,041 square kilometres of forest cover from 2013 to 2023, 24% of India's net gain.
facts.measure: Increase in forest cover 2013 to 2023
facts.compare: India net gain 16,630 sq km; Kerala 3,675; Karnataka 3,084; Andhra Pradesh has 5.0% of India's area
facts.stays_true: Same as the Kerala forest-growth fact: a fixed 2013-2023 pair, to be replaced when ISFR 2025 appears (expected about end-2026).
facts.lead: 366 sq km (10%) over Kerala
facts.size_effect: Andhra Pradesh holds 5.0% of India's land but gave 24% of the net gain.
facts.caution: Net gain: some States lost cover (Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Nagaland). Do not use with the Kerala forest-growth video on the same day. Andhra Pradesh 2013 is the post-bifurcation figure printed in the answer.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 3461, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 11.08.2025: "Tiger Reserve in Tamil Nadu"
facts.as_on: ISFR 2013 and ISFR 2023; answer dated 11 August 2025

facts.fact: Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Uttarakhand held 1,908 of India's 3,682 tigers in 2022, 52%, on 17% of its land.
facts.measure: Tigers (All India Tiger Estimation)
facts.compare: 785 + 563 + 560 = 1,908 of 3,682; the three states have 16.8% of India's area

facts.size_effect: 51.8% of tigers on 16.8% of land
facts.caution: Three states, one video: do not use on the same day as the Madhya Pradesh or Uttarakhand tiger facts.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 953, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 02.12.2024: "Decreasing Tiger Population"
facts.as_on: All India Tiger Estimation 2022; answer dated 2 December 2024

facts.fact: Uttarakhand has about 105 tigers per 10,000 km2, nearly double the next state, Kerala's 55, in the 2022 estimate.
facts.measure: Tigers per 10,000 km2 of state area
facts.compare: Kerala 54.8; Karnataka 29.4; Assam 29.2; Madhya Pradesh 25.5; India 11.2
facts.column: Tiger estimate 2022 / Geographical area (km2) (area from land_isfr2023_forest_tree_cover)
facts.source: NTCA and Wildlife Institute of India, Status of Tigers, Co-predators & Prey in India 2022, Table I.3.2; area from ISFR 2023 Table 2.4
facts.stays_true: Valid as a statement about the 2022 estimate. The sixth cycle (2026) is under way; a new report is likely to supersede it within about a year, so the figure may be restated.
facts.lead: 49.9 per 10,000 km2 (91%) over Kerala
facts.size_effect: A rate per area; Madhya Pradesh has the most tigers (785) but only 25.5 per 10,000 km2. State rows do not add to India (shared tigers) and West Bengal has no state row.
facts.caution: Rank holds only among the 18 state rows printed. West Bengal (Sundarbans landscape 101, northern WB 2) has no state row so it cannot be ranked. Our division of the report's estimate (SE 24) by the state's total area, not by tiger habitat.

facts.fact: Tree cover is 18.6% of Chandigarh's area, the highest of any state or UT; Delhi is next at 11.9% (ISFR 2023).
facts.measure: Tree cover (patches under 1 ha and scattered trees outside forest) as % of area
facts.compare: India 3.41%; Delhi 11.87%; Kerala 7.48%
facts.source: Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report 2023, Vol. 1, Table 2.4 (also stated in the text of section 2.10.4)
facts.stays_true: Chandigarh also led in ISFR 2021 (14.67% vs Delhi 11.53%). Tree cover is re-estimated each ISFR from sample plots; next edition ISFR 2025.
facts.lead: 6.71 points (57%) over Delhi; 2021: 3.13 points
facts.size_effect: Share of own area. A UT of 114 km2, so a small base: say 'state or UT'. J&K and Ladakh are left out (no separate area).
facts.caution: Tree cover is sample-plot based (ISFR prints standard errors in Table 2.13); 2023 tree cover includes bamboo and trees of 5-10 cm dbh. Do not add it to forest cover as 'forest'.

facts.fact: Goa has 52 km of coastline for every 1,000 km2 of land, more than three times Kerala's 15 km (revised 2025 coastline).
facts.measure: Coastline length per 1,000 km2 of state area
facts.compare: Kerala 15.4; Gujarat 11.9; Tamil Nadu 8.2; Maharashtra 2.9
facts.column: Revised coastline, 2025 (km) / Geographical area (km2) (area from land_isfr2023_forest_tree_cover)
facts.source: Survey of India / Ministry of Earth Sciences (coastline); Forest Survey of India ISFR 2023 Table 2.4 (area)
facts.as_on: Coastline promulgated 29 April 2025; areas as in ISFR 2023
facts.stays_true: Both inputs are fixed until the next coastline review (about 2035).
facts.lead: 36.9 km per 1,000 km2 (239%) over Kerala among states
facts.size_effect: This is a rate per area, built to remove size. Union territories Puducherry (87.0) and Daman and Diu, and the island UTs, are higher and left out of 'state'.
facts.caution: Our division of two official numbers; say 'among states'. Includes the revision (old Goa figure 160.50 km gives 43.4 per 1,000 km2, still the highest state).

facts.fact: Karnataka has 506 centrally protected monuments, more than any State but Uttar Pradesh, 13.7% of India's 3,685.
facts.measure: Centrally protected monuments and sites (ASI)
facts.compare: 13.7% of India's monuments against 5.0% of its people and 5.8% of its land (Census 2011); 2.7x its population share
facts.source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 84, 1 Dec 2025, Annexure-I (ASI figures); cross-checked with ASI list PDF CPM_List.pdf (created 8 Apr 2025)
facts.stays_true: Changes by a few when a site is notified or de-notified (Karnataka was 506 in both the April 2025 ASI list and the December 2025 answer); Goa 21 likewise; no fixed schedule.
facts.lead: 94 ahead of Tamil Nadu (23% more); Uttar Pradesh is first with 735 (743 in the April 2025 list)
facts.size_effect: Karnataka is 5.0% of India's people, so its 13.7% share is 2.7x its population share. ASI keeps three circles here (Bangalore, Dharwad, Hampi).
facts.caution: Centrally protected only. Second place needs the 3% / 1 point rule vs Tamil Nadu (met).

facts.fact: West Bengal holds 2,119 km2 of India's 4,992 km2 of mangroves, 42%; Gujarat is next with 1,164 km2 (ISFR 2023).
facts.measure: Mangrove cover
facts.compare: 42.45% of India's 4991.68 km2, while West Bengal is 2.7% of India's area; Gujarat 1164.06 km2
facts.source: Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report 2023, Vol. 1, Table 3.3
facts.stays_true: West Bengal held 2,117.75 km2 in 2021 and 2,119.16 km2 in 2023 (about 42% both times); the Sundarbans make the gap structural. Next edition ISFR 2025.
facts.size_effect: Not a size effect: Gujarat is 2.2 times larger and has a longer coast (2,340.62 km vs 721.02 km after the 2025 revision).
facts.caution: The report says nothing about causes; do not name the Sundarbans as the reason unless cited separately (it is a fact outside this table). Mangrove cover is a raster-based satellite estimate.

facts.fact: 85% of Mizoram's land is forest cover, the most of any State; India's average is 22% (ISFR 2023).
facts.measure: Forest cover as a share of geographical area
facts.compare: India 21.76%; Arunachal Pradesh 78.67%; Meghalaya 75.65%
facts.stays_true: Cross-check: the Forest Survey of India's own ISFR 2023 Table 2.4 (saved by the land collector as evergreen/land_isfr2023_forest_tree_cover) has the same forest-cover areas. The Forest Survey of India publishes the State of Forest Report every two years: ISFR 2023 came out on 21 December 2024 (Lok Sabha Q 981), so ISFR 2025 is the next edition and should be due about end-2026. State shares move by under one point an edition. RBI Handbook Table 99 gives the same top two (Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh) in every edition from 2015 to 2023.
facts.lead: 6.67 points (8.5%) over Arunachal Pradesh; the RBI Handbook series (Table 99 over geographical area) keeps Mizoram first among States by 5.4 to 8.6 points in 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2023
facts.size_effect: A share of the state's own land.
facts.caution: Lakshadweep (91%) is a Union Territory and higher: say 'any State'. 'Forest cover' is the Survey's mapped canopy (over 10% density, 1 ha or more) and includes plantations and orchards, not only recorded forest.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 304, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 02.02.2026: "Expansion of Forest Area in the Country"
facts.why: the same Forest Survey figure, from a Lok Sabha answer

facts.fact: Maharashtra has 7 of India's 45 UNESCO World Heritage properties, the most of any State; Tamil Nadu has 5.
facts.measure: UNESCO World Heritage properties (a shared property counted once under each State)
facts.compare: Tamil Nadu 5; Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Gujarat, Rajasthan 4 each; Maharashtra is 9.3% of India's people
facts.column: World Heritage properties (counted under each State/UT named)
facts.source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, India page (Internet Archive capture 12 Oct 2026) and data.unesco.org dataset whc001; State from Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3591 of 11 Aug 2025, Annexure-I
facts.stays_true: Changes when UNESCO's World Heritage Committee inscribes a new property at its yearly session; the next session's decisions are the next change.
facts.lead: 2 ahead (40% more) than Tamil Nadu; same lead on the 44-property list of Aug 2025
facts.size_effect: Maharashtra holds 15.6% of properties with 9.3% of people (1.7x): modest, so rank is the story, not size.
facts.caution: Six of the seven are cultural plus the shared natural Western Ghats; the Maratha Military Landscapes (2025) and Western Ghats (2012) are shared with Tamil Nadu. Counting shared properties once under each State is stated in the table.

facts.fact: Maharashtra's tigers rose from 103 in 2006 to 444 in 2022, 4.3 times; India's rose 2.6 times.
facts.measure: Tigers (All India Tiger Estimation)
facts.stays_true: The Government calls the Estimation quadrennial (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022); the next cycle's figures are not on the drive and would be a new count. facts.lead: Not a rank claim
facts.size_effect: Growth ratio against India's own ratio.

facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 953, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 02.12.2024: "Decreasing Tiger Population"

facts.fact: Assam holds 2 of India's 7 natural World Heritage sites, Kaziranga and Manas, on 2.4% of India's land.
facts.measure: Natural World Heritage properties
facts.compare: 29% of India's natural properties; Assam is 2.4% of area and 2.6% of people; every other State holds at most 1
facts.source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, India page (Internet Archive capture 12 Oct 2026) and data.unesco.org dataset whc001; State from Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3591 of 11 Aug 2025, Annexure-I
facts.stays_true: Natural inscriptions are rare (latest 2014 Great Himalayan National Park, 2016 Khangchendzonga as mixed); changes only if UNESCO inscribes another natural property.
facts.lead: 2 against a maximum of 1 for any other State (Western Ghats is one property shared by four States)
facts.size_effect: Assam is 2.4% of India's land, and the share of natural properties is 12x that.
facts.caution: Khangchendzonga (Sikkim) is listed as mixed, so is not counted as natural here. Assam's third property, Moidams (2024), is cultural.

facts.fact: Uttarakhand has 560 of India's 3,682 tigers, 15% of them, on 1.6% of India's area (2022 estimate).
facts.measure: Share of India's estimated tigers
facts.compare: 1.63% of India's area (9.3 times); Maharashtra has 444 on 9.4% of area
facts.source: NTCA and Wildlife Institute of India, Status of Tigers, Co-predators & Prey in India 2022, Table I.3.2; area from ISFR 2023 Table 2.4
facts.stays_true: As land-14: tied to the 2022 estimate; next report likely within about a year.
facts.lead: No rank claimed (Uttarakhand is third by count behind Madhya Pradesh 785 and Karnataka 563).
facts.size_effect: Compares the state's share of tigers with its share of area, so the large states are not favoured.
facts.caution: State rows do not add to the national estimate (3,682, SE 243) because tigers shared between states and outside protected areas are counted once at national level; the share is approximate. Overlaps with land-14; use one of them.

facts.fact: Chhattisgarh covers 4% more area than Tamil Nadu, yet Tamil Nadu had 2.8 times its people in Census 2011.
facts.measure: Area and population, Chhattisgarh against Tamil Nadu
facts.compare: Tamil Nadu 72,147,030 people on 130,060 sq km; Chhattisgarh 25,545,198 on 135,192 sq km
facts.source: Census of India 2011, Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India, Table A-01 (Number of villages, towns, households, population and area), read 13 Oct 2026
facts.stays_true: Area (Survey of India) and the 2011 count are fixed; population has grown since, so say 'in Census 2011'.
facts.lead: n/a (pair, not a rank)
facts.size_effect: The pair is chosen for near-equal area (3.9% apart); the gap is in people.
facts.caution: Population is Census 2011, not today's. Area is the Census/Survey of India figure. Do not rank the two States on anything but this size contrast. Pair: also Himachal Pradesh and Punjab (10.5% apart in area; Punjab had 4.0 times the people).

facts.fact: Karnataka has 69 colleges for every lakh people aged 18 to 23, more than twice India's 32 (AISHE 2023-24).
facts.measure: Colleges per lakh population aged 18-23
facts.compare: India 32; Telangana 56, Himachal Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh 51. Karnataka has 4,529 colleges.
facts.source: Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education: All India Survey on Higher Education 2023-24, Table 4 (page T-4)
facts.stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'.
facts.lead: 13 points (23%) over Telangana among states; in 2022-23 68 against 54 (Telangana)
facts.size_effect: A rate per head of the college-age population, so state size is divided out.
facts.caution: Of any state: Lakshadweep (60) and Puducherry (58, and 79 in 2022-23) are union territories; Puducherry was above Karnataka in 2022-23, so do not say 'state or UT'. The rate is AISHE's own, from its estimate of the 18-23 population.

facts.fact: Half of Goa's people (50.8%) knew three or more languages in Census 2011; for India the share was 7.1%.
facts.measure: Persons returning two languages besides their mother tongue, as a share of the population
facts.compare: India 7.1%; next Chandigarh 30.5%, Arunachal Pradesh 30.2%
facts.column: Share knowing three or more languages (%) [derived]
facts.source: Census of India 2011, Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India, Tables C-17 (bilingualism and trilingualism) and C-16 (mother tongue), read 13 Oct 2026
facts.stays_true: Census 2011 count; next census results expected from 2027.
facts.lead: 50.82% against Chandigarh 30.51% (20.3 points, 67% more). Census 2001 (checked): Goa 47.84% against Chandigarh 37.55%
facts.size_effect: A share of the State's own people.
facts.caution: 'Three or more languages' = the mother tongue plus two more, as Table C-17 counts. Say 'said they knew'. Pairs with the previous fact; use one or the other in a video.

facts.fact: Kerala has about 72 wild elephants per 1,000 km2, the highest density of any state; Assam has 53 (2021-25 DNA-based estimate).
facts.measure: Wild elephants per 1,000 km2 of state area
facts.compare: Assam 53.0; Uttarakhand 33.5; Karnataka 31.4; India 6.8; Kerala has 12.4% of India's elephants on 1.18% of its area
facts.column: Elephant population estimate (number) / Geographical area (km2) (area from land_isfr2023_forest_tree_cover)
facts.source: Wildlife Institute of India, Status of Elephants in India: DNA based SAIEE 2021-2025, Table E.1; area from ISFR 2023 Table 2.4
facts.stays_true: The report calls it a new baseline and expects calibrated methods in future; no next national estimate date is printed, but state-level surveys may be reported meanwhile. Confirm there is no newer release.
facts.lead: 18.7 per 1,000 km2 (35%) over Assam
facts.size_effect: A rate per area, so Karnataka's larger count does not decide it.
facts.caution: PROVENANCE: the report was read from Mongabay India's hosted copy of the Wildlife Institute of India's PDF, not from wii.gov.in or the Ministry (not found there); confirm before use. The report says the DNA-based figures are not comparable with the 2017 census: no 'decline' claims. Estimate has wide intervals (Kerala 2,378 to 3,193).

facts.fact: In Census 2011, 77.2% of Goa's people said they knew two or more languages; the figure for India was 26.0%.
facts.measure: Persons returning at least one language besides their mother tongue, as a share of the population
facts.compare: India 26.0%; next Andaman and Nicobar Islands 67.6%; next State Arunachal Pradesh 64.0%
facts.column: Share knowing two or more languages (%) [derived]
facts.source: Census of India 2011, Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India, Tables C-17 (bilingualism and trilingualism) and C-16 (mother tongue), read 13 Oct 2026
facts.stays_true: Census 2011 count; the next census (results expected from 2027) will carry a new language question and tables.
facts.lead: 77.21% against Andaman and Nicobar Islands 67.64% (9.6 points, 14% more) and Arunachal Pradesh 64.03%. Census 2001 (checked, all 35 State/UT files): Goa 73.36% against Andaman and Nicobar Islands 65.54%
facts.size_effect: A share of the State's own people; Goa is small but the lead is a rate.
facts.caution: Language knowledge is what the respondent reported (a mother tongue plus up to two other languages) in Table C-17. State the count only; no ranking of languages or States' worth. Do not publish a 'lowest' version of this fact.

facts.fact: Forest covers 85.3% of Mizoram, the highest share of any state; across India it is 21.8% (ISFR 2023).
facts.measure: Forest cover as % of the state's geographical area
facts.compare: India 21.76%; next state Arunachal Pradesh 78.67%; ISFR 2021: Mizoram 84.19%, Arunachal 78.78%
facts.source: Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report 2023, Vol. 1, Table 2.4 (Forest Survey of India, MoEFCC)
facts.stays_true: Rank holds in ISFR 2021 and 2023 with a gap of about 6 points; decimals move with each biennial report (ISFR 2025 is the next, due about two years after ISFR 2023).
facts.lead: 6.67 points (8.5%) over Arunachal Pradesh; same lead in 2021 (5.41 points)
facts.size_effect: Share of the state's own area, so size does not drive it. Lakshadweep (UT, 91.33% of 29.63 km2) and A&N Islands (UT, 81.62%) are not states and are left out of the rank.
facts.caution: FSI 'forest cover' means tree canopy of 1 hectare or more at 10%+ density whatever the land's legal status; it includes plantations, orchards, rubber and bamboo, so say 'forest cover', not 'natural forest'.

facts.fact: Manipur has 212,481 handloom weavers: about one for every 15 people, 34 times India's rate, in the 2019-20 handloom census.
facts.measure: Handloom weavers per 1,000 people
facts.compare: India 2.0 per 1,000; next Arunachal Pradesh 51.1, then Assam 31.9; Manipur has 7.9% of India's weavers and 0.23% of its people
facts.source: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles, Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20, Annexure II Tables 1-2 (handlooms.nic.in/assets/img/Statistics/3736.pdf); projected population (Population Projections 2011-2036, MoHFW, July 2020)
facts.stays_true: A census of 2019-20; it changes only when the Fifth Handloom Census is published (no date announced as far as we found).
facts.lead: 33% above Arunachal Pradesh; in the 2009-10 census Manipur also led (adult weavers 200,607 on Census 2011 population 2,855,794 = 70 per 1,000, Assam 45)
facts.size_effect: A rate per person, so population size is removed. A small State leads.
facts.caution: 'Weavers' as defined by the census (not allied workers). Population is the official projection for 1 March 2020, printed as 'projected population'. Assam's raw lead (11 lakh weavers) is already in Short fa06.

facts.fact: West Bengal's 2,216.7 km border with Bangladesh is 54% of that whole border and longer than India's entire Nepal border (1,751 km).
facts.measure: Land border with Bangladesh
facts.compare: 54.1% of the 4096.7 km India-Bangladesh border; India-Nepal border 1,751.0 km; India-Myanmar 1,643.0 km; next state Tripura 856 km
facts.source: Ministry of Home Affairs, Annual Report 2024-25, Chapter 3 paras 3.5 and 3.9 (length source: Survey of India)
facts.stays_true: Boundary lengths are Survey of India figures that change only by a treaty or survey correction; the report gives the same split for each year.
facts.lead: 2.6 times Tripura (856 km), the next state on this border
facts.size_effect: Border length, not area; West Bengal's border share is 54% while its area share is 2.7%.
facts.caution: Only the Bangladesh and Myanmar borders have state-wise lengths in this report; do not say West Bengal has the longest land border of any state (Nepal and Bhutan lengths are not split by state). Use 'longest Bangladesh border'.

facts.fact: Bamboo-bearing forest in Tripura spans 4,466 km2, equal to 42.6% of the state's area; India's figure is 4.7%.
facts.measure: Bamboo bearing area (inside recorded forest area) as % of state area
facts.compare: India 4.7%; Manipur 33.67%; Nagaland 24.01%
facts.column: Bamboo bearing area, ISFR 2023 (km2) / Geographical area (km2) (from land_isfr2023_forest_tree_cover)
facts.source: Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report 2023, Vol. 1, Chapter 5 'Bamboo Bearing Area' table; area from Table 2.4
facts.stays_true: Tripura also led in ISFR 2021 (40.06% vs Manipur 37.52%); the gap widened in 2023. Plot-based estimate re-made each ISFR; next edition ISFR 2025.
facts.lead: 8.92 points (27%) over Manipur; 2021 gap 2.54 points (6.8%)
facts.size_effect: Share of own area, so Madhya Pradesh (20,421 km2, largest in absolute terms) does not lead.
facts.caution: ISFR's bamboo area is measured in sample plots inside recorded forest area only and is not printed as a share of state area: the percentage is our division (numerator inside forest, denominator the whole state). Say 'bamboo-bearing forest area'. Estimates from sample plots with no error printed.

facts.fact: Maharashtra holds 2,696 of India's 6,628 specified dams, 40.7 per cent, on 9.4 per cent of the country's area (April 2025).
facts.measure: Specified dams (completed and under construction)
facts.compare: India 6,628; second state Madhya Pradesh 1,370. Maharashtra has 9.4% of India's area and 9.1% of its people (projected, 1 Mar 2025).
facts.source: National Dam Safety Authority, Ministry of Jal Shakti: National Register of Specified Dams, April 2025 (summary table, page iv)
facts.stays_true: Counts change only when dams are completed or added to the register; the register is re-issued every few years (2023, then April 2025). The April 2025 figures stay true as dated. Next edition date not announced.
facts.lead: 1,326 dams (1.97x) over Madhya Pradesh, 97% more
facts.size_effect: Not a size effect: share of dams 40.7% against 9.4% of area and 9.1% of people; Madhya Pradesh has the same area share (9.4%) with half the dams.
facts.caution: Counts 'specified dams' under the Dam Safety Act 2021 (above 15 m, or 10-15 m with size conditions), compiled from state dam safety organisations; many are small tanks and earthen dams, not big-river dams. Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu have no entry. The 2023 register (6,138 completed dams) could not be fetched from the publisher, so the lead is checked against the 2025 edition only.

facts.fact: Madhya Pradesh has 127 Kendriya Vidyalayas sanctioned, twice Maharashtra's 63, with 69% of Maharashtra's people (December 2025).
facts.measure: Kendriya Vidyalayas sanctioned
facts.compare: India 1,405; Uttar Pradesh 134; Odisha 82; Maharashtra 63; Tamil Nadu 49; Madhya Pradesh 6.3% of projected population (1 March 2026)
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 67, Education, answered 01.12.2025: "Regional Languages in KVs and JNVs"
facts.stays_true: Kendriya Vidyalayas are sanctioned in batches by the Union Cabinet (a few dozen a year); the Madhya Pradesh to Maharashtra ratio would need 60+ new schools in Maharashtra to change. This is the newest KV-by-state count on the drive; the 20 July 2026 answer (Q 69) gives computers per student, not school counts.
facts.lead: Second to Uttar Pradesh (134); no rank claimed
facts.size_effect: Schools per person: Madhya Pradesh 1.42 per million against Maharashtra 0.49.
facts.caution: 'Sanctioned', not necessarily open; KVs mainly serve children of transferable Central Government and defence staff (reply (b)), so counts follow defence and Central offices, not population. Say so on screen; no judgement about Maharashtra.

facts.fact: Maharashtra has 2,713 of India's 6,598 specified dams, 41%, on 9% of the land (pre-monsoon 2026).
facts.measure: Completed and operational specified dams under the Dam Safety Act, 2021
facts.compare: India 6,598; next state Madhya Pradesh 1,370 (Maharashtra has 1.98 times as many); Maharashtra has 9.4% of India's geographical area and 9.1% of projected population (1 March 2026); 8.8 dams per 1,000 sq km against India's 2.0
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 3066, Jal Shakti, answered 06.08.2026: "Safety Assessments for Dams and Reservoirs"
facts.stays_true: The count moves by a few dozen a year as dams are completed (dams inspected before the monsoon: 6,366 in 2024, 6,543 in 2025 as on 8 Dec, 6,566 of 6,598 in 2026, per Lok Sabha Q 2028 of 11 Dec 2025 and Q 3066). Maharashtra's lead of over 1,300 dams cannot close. This is the newest answer on the drive (ls_find dam); NDSA published its National Register of Specified Dams in April 2025. Next: the post-monsoon 2026 / pre-monsoon 2027 inspection count.
facts.lead: 1,343 dams (98%) over Madhya Pradesh
facts.size_effect: Maharashtra has 9.4% of the land and 9.1% of the people but 41.1% of the dams; dams per sq km is 4.5 times India's.
facts.caution: 'Specified dam' is a legal class under the Dam Safety Act (our reading: height above 15 m, or 10 to 15 m with extra conditions); it is not every dam and not a measure of water stored. Do not link to irrigation.
facts.why: the same claim on a newer count: 2,713 of 6,598 in a Lok Sabha answer of Aug 2026. Re-read both before a script.

facts.fact: Tamil Nadu has 412 of India's 3,685 centrally protected monuments, 11% of them, on 4% of India's land.
facts.measure: Centrally protected monuments and sites (ASI)
facts.compare: Share of monuments 11.2% against 4.0% of area and 6.0% of people (Census 2011); 2.8x its area share
facts.source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 84, 1 Dec 2025, Annexure-I (ASI figures); cross-checked with ASI list PDF CPM_List.pdf (created 8 Apr 2025)
facts.stays_true: Changes by a few when a site is notified or de-notified (Tamil Nadu was 412 in both the April 2025 ASI list and the December 2025 Parliament answer); no fixed schedule.
facts.lead: Third among States/UTs (Uttar Pradesh 735, Karnataka 506); no first-place claim
facts.size_effect: Share of monuments is 2.8x its area share and 1.9x its population share, so size does not explain it.
facts.caution: Centrally protected only; state-protected monuments are separate and not in this table.

facts.fact: Gujarat has the longest coastline of any state, 2,340.62 km, after the 2025 revision; it was 1,214.70 km before.
facts.measure: Length of coastline (revised, High-Water Line, 1:250,000)
facts.compare: 21.1% of India's 11098.81 km, from 5.97% of India's area; next state Tamil Nadu 1068.69 km; old Gujarat figure 1214.7 km
facts.source: Survey of India note 'Length of Coastline of India' (NHO with SoI); Ministry of Earth Sciences, Parliament answer 'Coastline of the Country', PIB 4 Dec 2025
facts.as_on: Revised length promulgated 29 April 2025; Parliament answer 4 December 2025
facts.stays_true: The Government will review the length on a 10-year cycle (Terms of Reference item f), so the next review is about 2035.
facts.lead: 1271.93 km (119%) over Tamil Nadu
facts.size_effect: Coast length is not area; Gujarat's coast share (21.1%) is 3.5 times its area share (6.0%). Andaman and Nicobar Islands (UT) is longer (3,083.50 km) and is left out of 'state'.
facts.caution: Do not say Gujarat's coast 'grew'; the Survey of India says the gap to the old figure is due to scale and method (1:250,000 maps against 1:4,500,000, modern GIS, offshore islands added). Use 'recalculated'.

facts.fact: Tripura, 10,486 km2, shares 856 km of border with Bangladesh; Assam, 7.5 times larger, shares only 263 km.
facts.measure: Land border with Bangladesh
facts.compare: Assam 263 km (7.48 times Tripura's area); per 1,000 km2: Tripura 81.6, West Bengal 25.0, Meghalaya 19.8, Mizoram 15.1, Assam 3.4
facts.source: Ministry of Home Affairs, Annual Report 2024-25, Chapter 3 para 3.9 (Survey of India); area from ISFR 2023 Table 2.4
facts.stays_true: Border lengths are fixed Survey of India figures; Tripura's and Assam's areas are fixed.
facts.lead: Tripura's border is 3.25 times Assam's; Tripura's border per area is 3.3 times West Bengal's
facts.size_effect: This is the surprise: a small state with a longer border than a state 7.5 times larger.
facts.caution: Assam's border also runs with Bhutan (length not split by state in the report); the claim is only about the Bangladesh border.

facts.fact: Maharashtra has 2,696 specified dams; Rajasthan, 11 per cent larger in area, has 315 (National Register, April 2025).

facts.compare: Rajasthan 315 dams on 342,239 sq km; Maharashtra 2,696 dams on 307,713 sq km; ratio 8.6x
facts.source: National Dam Safety Authority, Ministry of Jal Shakti: National Register of Specified Dams, April 2025 (summary table, page iv)
facts.stays_true: Counts change only when dams are completed or added to the register; the register is re-issued every few years (2023, then April 2025). The April 2025 figures stay true as dated. Next edition date not announced.
facts.lead: 8.6x Rajasthan
facts.size_effect: Two states of similar size far apart: Rajasthan is 11% larger in area (342,239 vs 307,713 sq km, ISFR 2023) and has 11.7% of Maharashtra's dams.
facts.caution: Counts 'specified dams' under the Dam Safety Act 2021 (above 15 m, or 10-15 m with size conditions), compiled from state dam safety organisations; many are small tanks and earthen dams, not big-river dams. Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu have no entry. The 2023 register (6,138 completed dams) could not be fetched from the publisher, so the lead is checked against the 2025 edition only. Do not use in the same video as built-01 (same table, same state).

facts.fact: Goa, India's smallest state at 3,702 km2, has forest cover on 61.2% of its area, against 21.8% for India (ISFR 2023).
facts.measure: Forest cover as % of state area
facts.compare: India 21.76%; Kerala 56.78%; Goa is 2.8 times India
facts.source: Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report 2023, Vol. 1, Table 2.4
facts.stays_true: Goa's share has been about 61% in both ISFR 2021 (61.24%) and 2023 (61.20%); next edition ISFR 2025.
facts.lead: No rank claimed beyond being above Kerala (56.78%) by 4.4 points.
facts.size_effect: Smallest state by area, picked because a small state has a large share; share is of own area.
facts.caution: Forest cover counts cashew, coconut and other plantations as well as natural forest; do not call it all 'forest'. Goa is the smallest state by area (3,702 km2, ISFR Table 2.4).

facts.fact: Maharashtra has 434 of India's 1,330 functional urban cooperative banks, 33%, nearly twice Karnataka's 237 (March 2026).
facts.measure: Functional urban cooperative banks
facts.compare: India 1,330; Karnataka 237; Gujarat 203; Tamil Nadu 102; Maharashtra 9.1% of projected population (1 March 2026)
facts.stays_true: Urban cooperative banks are licensed and merged by RBI over years, so the count drifts by a few a year Only one State-wise count of urban cooperative banks was read (Q 2939, 10 Mar 2026, the newest on the drive); it was not cross-checked against RBI's own list of UCBs, which is the publisher to read before posting.
facts.lead: 197 banks (83%) over Karnataka; 14.8 points
facts.size_effect: 32.6% of banks against 9.1% of people.
facts.caution: Banks, not branches or deposits. A Short about cooperative banks must not imply anything about the trouble some UCBs have had.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2939, Cooperation, answered 10.03.2026: "Cooperative Banks and Cooperative Societies"
facts.as_on: National Cooperative Database as of 1 March 2026; answer dated 10 March 2026

facts.fact: Tamil Nadu has 242 companies mining major minerals, more than twice Odisha's 104, among 1,650 in India (March 2026).
facts.measure: Companies operating in mining (major minerals, excluding coal and lignite)
facts.compare: India 1,650; Andhra Pradesh 282; Madhya Pradesh 278; Karnataka 183; Odisha 104; Jharkhand 56
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 5424, Mines, answered 25.03.2026: "Mining Companies in the Country"
facts.as_on: Lok Sabha answer of 25 March 2026 (Indian Bureau of Mines data)
facts.stays_true: Mining leases and companies change every year; only one answer on the drive (ls_find mining). A newer Indian Bureau of Mines list would replace it.
facts.lead: Third (Andhra Pradesh 282, Madhya Pradesh 278, Tamil Nadu 242): no rank claimed
facts.size_effect: 14.7% of companies against 5.4% of the people.
facts.caution: A count of companies, not tonnes, mines or value: Odisha and Jharkhand lead in output. Excludes coal and lignite and minor minerals (sand, stone). Weak: leave out unless AK wants a mining story.

facts.fact: Kerala has 665 km of road per 100 square kilometres, the most of any State and 4.0 times India's 166 (2020).
facts.measure: Road length per 100 sq km of land (all roads)
facts.compare: India 166; Assam 574; Goa 512; Kerala 258,375 km on 38,852 sq km
facts.source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Table 146 (from the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways); area from Lok Sabha Q 304 (ISFR 2023)
facts.stays_true: Kerala has been first among States in every Handbook year from 2015 to 2020 (5.0 to 6.7 km per sq km, Assam or Goa second). The Handbook's road series stops at 2020; a later Ministry year-book would replace it. The lead over Assam narrowed to 16% in 2020.
facts.lead: 91 km per 100 sq km (16%) over Assam; Union Territories Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry and Lakshadweep are higher
facts.size_effect: A rate per unit of land.
facts.caution: 'All roads' include village and urban roads; the Ministry's definitions changed in some States in 2013 to 2018 (Madhya Pradesh's total doubled), so compare only the order. Say 'any State', not 'in India'.

facts.fact: Sikkim has 11 universities for about 0.7 million people, 16 per million, against 0.9 per million across India (AISHE 2023-24).
facts.measure: Universities per million people
facts.compare: India 0.91; Ladakh (UT) 9.9; Arunachal Pradesh 6.9. Sikkim: 11 universities, projected population 702 thousand (1 Mar 2025).
facts.source: Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education: All India Survey on Higher Education 2023-24, Table 1 (page T-1)
facts.stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'. The population is a projection; Census 2011 gave 6.1 lakh.
facts.lead: 1.6x Ladakh, 2.3x Arunachal Pradesh, the next state; in 2022-23 Sikkim 15.7, next Ladakh 6.6
facts.size_effect: A rate per head. Small base: one more university moves the rate by 1.4. 8 of its 11 are state private universities.
facts.caution: Small state, small base. Population is the official projection for 1 March 2025 (about 702 thousand). Eight of the 11 are state private universities.

facts.fact: In the 2019-20 handloom census, 96 of every 100 Manipur weavers are women; Odisha 20, India 72.
facts.measure: Women as a share of handloom weavers
facts.compare: Odisha 20.2%, Karnataka 21.3%, Telangana 22.0%; India 71.6%; Assam 93.2%, Nagaland 94.1%
facts.source: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles, Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20, Annexure II Tables 1-2 (handlooms.nic.in/assets/img/Statistics/3736.pdf)
facts.stays_true: A census of 2019-20; changes with the Fifth Handloom Census.
facts.lead: No rank claim: Sikkim (96.8% of 632 weavers) is higher than Manipur (96.2%), and Nagaland is within 3% of it
facts.size_effect: A share, not a count.
facts.caution: Do not rank; use as a contrast between regions. 'Weavers' excludes allied workers. In the 2009-10 census Odisha was 15% and Haryana, Delhi, Chhattisgarh lower, so Odisha is not 'lowest' there.

facts.fact: Madhya Pradesh (308,252 km2) and Maharashtra (307,713 km2) match in size, but Maharashtra had 1.55 times the people in Census 2011.
facts.measure: Geographical area; population (Census 2011, 1 March 2011)
facts.compare: Area differs by 539 km2 (0.18%); Census 2011 population Maharashtra 112,374,000, Madhya Pradesh 72,627,000 (1.547 times)

facts.as_on: Area as in ISFR 2023; population counts as on 1 March 2011
facts.stays_true: Areas are fixed; the Census 2027 count will replace the 2011 populations once released (state this as 'in Census 2011').
facts.lead: MP larger by 539.11 km2 (0.18%); Maharashtra's population 55% higher
facts.size_effect: This is two states of the same size far apart on people, the shape the brief asks for.
facts.caution: Population is a count as on 1 March 2011, not a current figure (the projection report's 2011 column is the Census). Madhya Pradesh's area is 308,252.11 km2 in ISFR (after Chhattisgarh split, as printed).

facts.fact: Three States were born within 15 days in November 2000: Chhattisgarh (1st), Uttarakhand (9th) and Jharkhand (15th).
facts.measure: Appointed days of the Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar Reorganisation Acts, 2000

facts.source: The Constitution of India as on 1 May 2024, First Schedule entries 25-27 and footnotes (Acts 28, 29 and 30 of 2000), Ministry of Law and Justice, Legislative Department
facts.stays_true: Dates in law do not change.

facts.size_effect: A date, not a size.
