facts.fact: Gujarat has 65 of India's 464 state private universities, 14 per cent, with 5.2 per cent of the people (AISHE 2023-24).
facts.measure: State private universities
facts.compare: India 464; Madhya Pradesh 52, Rajasthan 50. Gujarat has 5.2% of India's people (projected, 1 Mar 2025).
facts.source: Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education: All India Survey on Higher Education 2023-24, Table 1 (page T-1)
facts.stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'.
facts.lead: 13 (25%) over Madhya Pradesh; in 2022-23 60 against 49 (Rajasthan)
facts.size_effect: Share of private universities 14.0% against 5.2% of people and 6.0% of area.
facts.caution: Counts state private universities only (one of ten university types). Registered in AISHE does not say how many students each enrols. Do not use with built-12 in one video.

facts.fact: Tamil Nadu has 26 of India's 82 private deemed universities, 32 per cent, with 5.5 per cent of the people (AISHE 2023-24).
facts.measure: Deemed universities, private
facts.compare: India 82; Karnataka 12, Maharashtra 11.
facts.source: Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education: All India Survey on Higher Education 2023-24, Table 1 (page T-1)
facts.stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'.
facts.lead: 14 (2.2x) over Karnataka; in 2022-23 26 of 81 against Karnataka's 12
facts.size_effect: Share 31.7% against 5.5% of people and 4.0% of area.
facts.caution: 'Deemed university' is a status granted by the central government; 'private' is the AISHE management category. Say what it counts: 26 institutions.

facts.fact: Every hectare of Punjab's sown land is irrigated: 4,109 of 4,109 thousand hectares in 2023-24, against 59% for India.
facts.measure: Net irrigated area as a share of net sown area
facts.source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Tables 54 and 56 (from Land Use Statistics at a Glance, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare)
facts.stays_true: Land-use statistics are annual and slow: Punjab has been 96% to 100% since 2004-05. RBI's Handbook is published yearly (the 2023-24 figures are provisional and may be revised in the next Handbook, about autumn 2027 for 2024-25).
facts.lead: 8.3 points (9%) over Haryana, the next State
facts.size_effect: A share within the state's own sown land.
facts.caution: Provisional; 'net irrigated' means irrigated by any source once, as the Ministry reports it. Equal values in the two tables are as printed; say 'reported'. Well-known; the surprise is the exactness, and the 41-point gap to India.

facts.fact: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands' coastline is 3,083.50 km, 28% of India's, though the islands are 0.25% of its area.
facts.measure: Length of coastline (revised 2025)
facts.compare: 27.78% of India's 11098.81 km; 0.251% of India's area; Gujarat 2340.62 km; old A&N figure 1,962.00 km
facts.source: Survey of India, 'Length of Coastline of India'; Ministry of Earth Sciences Parliament answer, PIB 4 Dec 2025
facts.stays_true: Next review of the coastline length is on a 10-year cycle (about 2035).
facts.lead: 742.88 km (32%) over Gujarat, the longest state; also longer than the old A&N figure 1,962.00 km
facts.size_effect: Island chains have long coasts for their area; this is the point of the fact, not a hidden size effect.
facts.caution: Coast of an island UT built from peripheral coastline of its islands (India has 1,298 offshore islands/islets in the reconciliation). Never compare with a mainland state's length without saying 'islands'.

facts.fact: Mizoram's 3 dams hold 1.94 billion cubic metres, 1.5 times the 1.29 held by West Bengal's 36 (April 2025).
facts.measure: Gross storage capacity of specified dams
facts.compare: West Bengal 1.287 BCM in 36 dams; Bihar 1.012 BCM in 28.
facts.source: National Dam Safety Authority, Ministry of Jal Shakti: National Register of Specified Dams, April 2025 (summary table, page iv)
facts.stays_true: Counts change only when dams are completed or added to the register; the register is re-issued every few years (2023, then April 2025). The April 2025 figures stay true as dated. Next edition date not announced.
facts.lead: Not a rank claim
facts.size_effect: Mizoram has 21,081 sq km, 24% of West Bengal's; storage per dam 646 vs 36 million cubic metres.
facts.caution: Counts 'specified dams' under the Dam Safety Act 2021 (above 15 m, or 10-15 m with size conditions), compiled from state dam safety organisations; many are small tanks and earthen dams, not big-river dams. Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu have no entry. The 2023 register (6,138 completed dams) could not be fetched from the publisher, so the lead is checked against the 2025 edition only. The register's list of important dams includes Mizoram's Tuirial dam (completed 2017); three dams is a very small base, so one new dam would change the comparison.

facts.fact: West Bengal has 47 railway route km per 1,000 sq km, 2.2 times India's 21, the highest of any state (March 2024).
facts.measure: Railway route km per 1,000 sq km of area
facts.compare: India 21.0; Punjab 45.0, Bihar 42.0, Haryana 40.3. West Bengal 4,161 route km on 88,752 sq km.
facts.source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25, Table 145 (data of the Ministry of Railways), 11 Dec 2025
facts.stays_true: Route length changes slowly (a new line or a gauge change adds or removes a few km); the Handbook is annual (the 2025-26 edition will carry end-March 2025). Density ranks have held since 2020.
facts.lead: 1.9 points (4.2%) over Punjab, the next state; in end-March 2020 it was 47.5 against Punjab's 45.0
facts.size_effect: Rate per area, so state size is divided out. Delhi (127) and Chandigarh (140) are higher and Puducherry (46.9) is level with it: say 'highest of any state', not 'of any state or UT'.
facts.caution: The Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 and Annual Statistical Statements 2024-25 give route length by zonal railway only, so the state split comes from the RBI Handbook, which prints the Ministry of Railways as its source. Area is ISFR 2023 geographical area (Forest Survey of India). Route km is the length of line open, not track km. The lead over Punjab is real but thin (4%).

facts.fact: In Census 2011, Kerala's 1,017 inhabited villages averaged 17,179 rural people each; India's average was 1,395.
facts.measure: Rural population per inhabited village (rural population divided by inhabited villages)
facts.compare: India 1,395; next State Tripura 3,143 (5.5 times lower); 12.3 times the India figure
facts.source: Census of India 2011, Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India, Table A-01 (Number of villages, towns, households, population and area), read 13 Oct 2026
facts.stays_true: Census 2011 counts do not change; the next census (results expected from 2027) will give new village counts and sizes.
facts.lead: 17,179 against Tripura 3,143 among States (447% more); Chandigarh (UT, 5 villages) 5,798. Census 2001 (checked): Kerala 17,283 against Tripura 3,093
facts.size_effect: A rate (rural people per village), not a count; Kerala has 2.8% of India's people but 0.17% of its inhabited villages.
facts.caution: The source states only counts; do not give a reason. Say 'villages as the Census counts them'. Use rural population only, not the whole State population.

facts.fact: Between the 2001 and 2011 censuses, Kerala's towns rose from 159 to 520 while its inhabited villages fell from 1,364 to 1,017.
facts.measure: Number of towns and inhabited villages, Census 2001 against Census 2011
facts.compare: Census 2001: 159 towns, 1,364 inhabited villages; Census 2011: 520 towns, 1,017 inhabited villages; India towns 5,161 to 7,933
facts.source: Census of India 2011, Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India, Table A-01 (Number of villages, towns, households, population and area), read 13 Oct 2026; Census of India 2001, Table A-01 (catalog 20028, read 13 Oct 2026)
facts.stays_true: Both are Census counts; the next census (results expected from 2027) adds a third point.
facts.lead: n/a (change over time, no rank claimed: West Bengal added more towns, 375 to 909)
facts.size_effect: A change in Kerala's own counts, not a size comparison.
facts.caution: Do not give a cause: the tables do not say why (Census towns are reclassified at each census by population, density and work-force rules). Say 'counted as towns'. The 2001 figures are in table evergreen/census2001_a1_states.

facts.fact: Kerala had 1,050 km of railway route in March 2004 and 1,048 km in March 2024; India's network grew 9.4 per cent.
facts.measure: Railway route length
facts.compare: India 63,221 km to 69,181 km (+5,960 km, +9.4%). Kerala still has 27.0 route km per 1,000 sq km against India's 21.0.
facts.source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25, Table 145 (data of the Ministry of Railways), 11 Dec 2025
facts.stays_true: Both dates are fixed so the statement stays true as dated; the end-March 2025 figure (next Handbook) could differ if a new line opens.
facts.lead: Not a rank claim
facts.size_effect: Not about size: Kerala's network is already dense (27.0 per 1,000 sq km, 1.3x India's), so there is little unserved area; the source gives no reason for the flat length.
facts.caution: The Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 and Annual Statistical Statements 2024-25 give route length by zonal railway only, so the state split comes from the RBI Handbook, which prints the Ministry of Railways as its source. Area is ISFR 2023 geographical area (Forest Survey of India). Route km is the length of line open, not track km. Gauge conversion and doubling add track km, not route km, so route km can stay flat while the lines are upgraded.

facts.fact: Andhra Pradesh has 350 of India's 1,547 notified marine fish landing centres, 23%, more than any other State (March 2026).
facts.measure: Notified marine fish landing centres
facts.compare: India 1,547; Tamil Nadu 301; Kerala 204; Maharashtra 173
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 3990, Fisheries, Animal Husbandry And Dairying , answered 17.03.2026: "Fish Landing Centres"
facts.stays_true: A State adds to this list when it notifies a new centre; the Ministry says the table is 'as reconciled by the States/UTs from time to time'. This is the only answer on the drive with notified-centre counts (the 24 Mar 2026 answer, Q 5201, is about funding). Tamil Nadu's 301 would need 50 more notifications to catch up.
facts.lead: 49 centres (16%) and 3.2 points over Tamil Nadu
facts.size_effect: Count, not rate. Per 100 km of the revised 2025 coastline (Survey of India / Ministry of Earth Sciences, saved by the land collector as evergreen/land_coastline_2025) Andhra Pradesh has 33.2 (350 on 1,053 km), Kerala 34.0 (204 on 600 km), Karnataka 33.5 and Tamil Nadu 28.2: so Andhra Pradesh leads in number, not per kilometre. Its coast (1,053 km) is about the same as Tamil Nadu's (1,069 km), so the 16% lead over Tamil Nadu is not a coast-length effect.
facts.caution: 'Notified' is the legal status, not 'built'. Only 380 of the 1,547 have been taken up for development, 301 completed. Do not describe quality or usage.

facts.fact: Kerala has 57% forest cover with 2.1 times India's people per square kilometre; India's forest cover is 22% (ISFR 2023).
facts.measure: Forest cover as a share of geographical area, against people per sq km
facts.compare: Kerala 932 projected people per sq km (1 March 2026) against India 434; India forest cover 21.76%; West Bengal (1,133 per sq km) has 18.97%
facts.stays_true: Cross-check: the Forest Survey of India's own ISFR 2023 Table 2.4 (saved by the land collector as evergreen/land_isfr2023_forest_tree_cover) has the same forest-cover areas. The Forest Survey of India publishes the State of Forest Report every two years: ISFR 2023 came out on 21 December 2024 (Lok Sabha Q 981), so ISFR 2025 is the next edition and should be due about end-2026. State shares move by under one point an edition. RBI Handbook Table 99 gives the same top two (Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh) in every edition from 2015 to 2023. Density uses the NCP projection for 1 March 2026 (state populations are projections, not a count).
facts.lead: Not a rank claim
facts.size_effect: Both measures are per unit of land.
facts.caution: Kerala's mapped forest cover includes plantations and tree-covered holdings; the Survey's definition is canopy, not natural forest. Print 'projected population' on screen. Do not say crowded people 'cause' forest.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 304, Environment, Forest And Climate Change, answered 02.02.2026: "Expansion of Forest Area in the Country"

facts.fact: Himachal Pradesh's 30 dams hold 19.5 billion cubic metres, 5.9% of India's storage, on 1.7% of its area (April 2025).
facts.measure: Gross storage capacity of specified dams
facts.compare: India 330.022 BCM; HP has 1.7% of India's area and 0.5% of its people (projected, 1 Mar 2025); 651 million cubic metres per dam against India's 50.
facts.source: National Dam Safety Authority, Ministry of Jal Shakti: National Register of Specified Dams, April 2025 (summary table, page iv)
facts.stays_true: Counts change only when dams are completed or added to the register; the register is re-issued every few years (2023, then April 2025). The April 2025 figures stay true as dated. Next edition date not announced.
facts.lead: Not a rank claim (Mizoram's 3 dams average 646 million m3 per dam, within 1% of HP's 651)
facts.size_effect: Share of storage 5.9% is 3.5x its share of area and 11.1x its share of people.
facts.caution: Counts 'specified dams' under the Dam Safety Act 2021 (above 15 m, or 10-15 m with size conditions), compiled from state dam safety organisations; many are small tanks and earthen dams, not big-river dams. Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu have no entry. The 2023 register (6,138 completed dams) could not be fetched from the publisher, so the lead is checked against the 2025 edition only. Built Short fa48 already uses Himachal Pradesh's large-hydro generation: this is reservoir capacity, a different measure, but avoid pairing the two. Includes Bhakra and Pong, which are managed by the BBMB.

facts.fact: Kerala's postal circle has 5,062 post offices, one per 7.7 sq km, against one per 19.9 sq km for India (March 2025).
facts.measure: Square km per post office (Kerala postal circle)
facts.compare: India 19.92 sq km per post office (India Post prints 19.92). West Bengal 9.8, Bihar 10.1 (state area over the circle's post offices).
facts.source: Department of Posts, reply to Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 4321, 18 Mar 2026, Annexure-I; India total and area per post office checked against India Post's Postal Network page (read 13 Oct 2026)
facts.stays_true: Post office counts change slowly (new branch offices in 2023-24, a few mergers); the answer is for 31 March 2025.
facts.lead: 1.27x: next densest single-state circle is West Bengal at 9.8 sq km per post office, so Kerala is 27% denser
facts.size_effect: Rate per area. Postal circles are not the same as states: Kerala circle is taken as Kerala plus Lakshadweep (area added), which the answer does not state.
facts.caution: CAUTION: the answer gives circles, not states, and does not say which states each circle covers. Delhi (2.9 sq km) is denser still. Needs the Department of Posts circle list before use.

facts.fact: India has 11 classical languages; five of them, Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali, were added on 3 October 2024.
facts.measure: Languages declared Classical Languages
facts.compare: Six before 2024: Tamil 2004, Sanskrit 2005, Telugu and Kannada 2008, Malayalam 2013, Odia 2014
facts.source: Ministry of Culture, 'Status of Classical Language: An Explainer', 4 Oct 2024 (PIB)
facts.stays_true: True as stated until the Union Cabinet adds another language; no schedule exists. Next edition: a new Ministry of Culture notification.
facts.lead: 5 of 11 on one date
facts.size_effect: Not a size matter.
facts.caution: The Ministry does not name a State per language; do not assign States in the script without a source. The Cabinet decision date is 3 Oct 2024; the explainer is dated 4 Oct.

facts.fact: Arunachal Pradesh is 7% larger than Assam by area, yet Assam had 22.6 times its people in Census 2011.
facts.measure: Area and population, Arunachal Pradesh against Assam
facts.compare: Assam 31,205,576 people on 78,438 sq km; Arunachal Pradesh 1,383,727 on 83,743 sq km
facts.source: Census of India 2011, Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India, Table A-01 (Number of villages, towns, households, population and area), read 13 Oct 2026
facts.stays_true: Census 2011 count and Survey of India area; population has grown since, so say 'in Census 2011'.
facts.lead: n/a (pair, not a rank)
facts.size_effect: The pair is chosen for near-equal area (6.8% apart); the gap is in people.
facts.caution: Area follows the Survey of India figure printed in the Census table (India's official map). Say 'Census area'. Population is Census 2011 only.

facts.fact: West Bengal has 47 km of railway route per 1,000 square kilometres, 2.2 times India's 21 (end-March 2024).
facts.measure: Railway route length per 1,000 sq km of land
facts.compare: India 21.0; Punjab 45.0; Bihar 42.0; Haryana 40.3; Kerala 27.0
facts.source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Table 145 (from the Ministry of Railways); area from Lok Sabha Q 304 (ISFR 2023)
facts.stays_true: The railway network grows slowly: West Bengal had 41.8 per 1,000 sq km in 2004, 45.9 in 2014 and 46.9 in 2024, India 21.0 in 2024. The next Handbook (about autumn 2027) adds end-March 2025.
facts.lead: No rank claimed: Punjab (45.0) is within 1.9 per 1,000 sq km, and in 2014 the two were within one
facts.size_effect: A rate per unit of land.
facts.caution: Route-km counts each line once whatever the number of tracks. Delhi and Chandigarh are higher (city UTs). Do not say 'highest'.

facts.fact: Tamil Nadu had 1,097 of India's 7,933 towns in Census 2011 (13.8%), with 6.0% of the country's people.
facts.measure: Number of towns (Census 2011)
facts.compare: 13.8% of India's towns against 6.0% of India's people; next State Uttar Pradesh 915
facts.source: Census of India 2011, Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India, Table A-01 (Number of villages, towns, households, population and area), read 13 Oct 2026
facts.stays_true: Census 2011 count. The next census (results expected from 2027) will recount towns and many more will be added or reclassified.
facts.lead: 1,097 against Uttar Pradesh 915 (20% more). Census 2001 (checked): Tamil Nadu 832 against Uttar Pradesh 704
facts.size_effect: Share of towns (13.8%) is 2.3 times the share of people (6.0%), so not a size effect; Uttar Pradesh has 16.5% of people but 11.5% of towns.
facts.caution: 'Towns' means statutory towns plus census towns, as in the A-01 table. Do not say 'cities'. India's printed total is 7,933 in this table; some Census summaries print 7,935.

facts.fact: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands had 97 wildlife sanctuaries in August 2023, 17% of India's 570; the next, Maharashtra, had 49.
facts.measure: Wildlife sanctuaries (number)
facts.compare: 17.0% of India's 570; 0.25% of India's area; Maharashtra 49; Karnataka 35; Tamil Nadu 33
facts.source: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Rajya Sabha written reply, PIB 10 Aug 2023, Annexure-I (National Wildlife Database Centre, Wildlife Institute of India)
facts.stays_true: A count that rises when sanctuaries are notified (a newer Parliament answer would give a higher total); the lead over the next state is large enough that the rank is unlikely to change, but recheck the count.
facts.lead: 48 sanctuaries (98%) over Maharashtra, the next
facts.size_effect: Counts of sanctuaries; many island sanctuaries are small, so say 'count', not 'area'. Per 1,000 km2, A&N has 11.8 against 0.16 for Maharashtra.
facts.caution: A count, not area; the reply prints no area. Data are for August 2023; a newer reply may have changed the figures. UT, not a state.

facts.fact: Maharashtra has 225,986 of India's 848,137 cooperative societies, 27%, with 9% of the people (March 2026).
facts.measure: Registered cooperative societies (all 30 sectors)
facts.compare: India 848,137; next state Gujarat 86,519 (2.6 times fewer); Maharashtra 9.1% of projected population (1 March 2026); functional societies 219,941 of 659,544
facts.stays_true: The National Cooperative Database is still being filled in: the 15 November 2025 version (Lok Sabha Q 1500) showed 845,187 societies and Maharashtra 224,732, the 1 March 2026 version 848,137 and 225,986, so the numbers move by about 1% in four months while the order does not. Newest on the drive: Q 2939 (10 Mar 2026). Next: the database's next update, no date given.
facts.lead: 2.6 times Gujarat; 16.4 points
facts.size_effect: 26.6% of societies against 9.1% of the people: 2.9 times.
facts.caution: Counts housing, dairy, credit, labour and other societies together; not members, not money. Housing societies are a big part of the count (India: 193,930 of 8.4 lakh in the Nov 2025 sector table). Say 'registered'.
facts.source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2939, Cooperation, answered 10.03.2026: "Cooperative Banks and Cooperative Societies"
facts.as_on: National Cooperative Database as of 1 March 2026; answer dated 10 March 2026

facts.fact: Maharashtra's National Highways grew from 6,249 km on 31 March 2014 to 18,462 km on 30 June 2025, third place to first.
facts.measure: Length of National Highways
facts.compare: x2.95 in 11 years; India 91,287 to 146,342 km (x1.60). Now 12.6% of India's NH length on 9.4% of its area. Uttar Pradesh was first in 2014 (7,986 km) and is second now (12,123).
facts.source: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, reply to Lok Sabha Starred Question 75, 24 July 2025, Annexure-I
facts.stays_true: Both dates are fixed, so the statement stays true as dated. National Highway length keeps changing as roads are notified and built, so the 'now' position can change in the next Parliament answer.
facts.lead: 6,339 km (1.52x) over Uttar Pradesh in 2025
facts.size_effect: Rank rise is from growth: 2014 length 6,249 km was 6.8% of India's; 2025 length is 12.6%. Area share unchanged at 9.4%.
facts.caution: National Highway length grows partly by notifying existing state roads as NHs: the same answer says about 54,004 km of state roads were notified as NHs since April 2014. Say 'length of notified National Highways', not 'new roads built'.

facts.fact: Karnataka has 6,013 of India's 22,446 wild elephants, 27% of them, from 5.8% of India's area (2021-25 DNA-based estimate).
facts.measure: Wild elephants (share of India)
facts.compare: 26.8% of India's 22446; 5.83% of India's area (4.6 times); Assam 4159
facts.source: Wildlife Institute of India, Status of Elephants in India: DNA based SAIEE 2021-2025, Table E.1; area from ISFR 2023 Table 2.4
facts.stays_true: As land-16: a new baseline; check for a newer release.
facts.lead: 1,854 elephants (45%) over Assam; confidence intervals overlap (Karnataka 4,792-7,235, Assam 3,395-4,924) only slightly
facts.size_effect: Compares share of elephants with share of area (4.6 times), so Karnataka's size does not explain it.
facts.caution: Same PROVENANCE and 'not comparable with 2017' cautions as land-16. Karnataka and Tamil Nadu also ran their own state counts (2023); do not mix.

facts.fact: Karnataka has 4,529 colleges, just over half of Uttar Pradesh's 8,625, with 29 per cent of its people (AISHE 2023-24).
facts.measure: Number of colleges
facts.compare: Uttar Pradesh 8,625 colleges, 240 million people; Karnataka 69 million (projected, 1 Mar 2025). Per lakh aged 18-23: Karnataka 69, Uttar Pradesh 31.
facts.source: Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education: All India Survey on Higher Education 2023-24, Table 4 (page T-4)
facts.stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'.
facts.lead: Not a rank claim (Uttar Pradesh has the most colleges; Karnataka is third after Maharashtra in count)
facts.size_effect: Karnataka has 53% of Uttar Pradesh's colleges and 29% of its people.
facts.caution: Overlaps built-16 (same table); use one. Count of colleges does not say size: average enrolment per college is 433 in Karnataka and 726 in Uttar Pradesh (Table 4).

facts.fact: Goa, India's smallest State by area, has 21 centrally protected monuments: 5.7 per 1,000 sq km against 1.1 for India.
facts.measure: Centrally protected monuments and sites per 1,000 sq km
facts.compare: India 1.12 per 1,000 sq km; Goa is 5.1x the national density; Goa area 3,702 sq km (Census 2011)
facts.source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 84, 1 Dec 2025, Annexure-I (ASI figures); cross-checked with ASI list PDF CPM_List.pdf (created 8 Apr 2025)
facts.stays_true: Changes by a few when a site is notified or de-notified (Karnataka was 506 in both the April 2025 ASI list and the December 2025 answer); Goa 21 likewise; no fixed schedule.
facts.lead: Third densest after Delhi and Puducherry (Goa 5.7; Puducherry 14.3; Delhi 115); no first claim
facts.size_effect: A density, so the small area is the point: the count (21) is itself small.
facts.caution: Same 21 in the April 2025 ASI list. Smallest State by area: Census 2011 areas Goa 3,702 sq km, Sikkim 7,096; UTs are smaller. Density uses Census 2011 area. Do not say 'densest'.

facts.fact: Sikkim, the second-smallest state at 7,096 km2, touches three countries, as do West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh, each about 12 times bigger.
facts.measure: Neighbouring countries touched by the state's land border (number)
facts.compare: Countries: China, Nepal, Bhutan. West Bengal (88,752 km2) and Arunachal Pradesh (83,743 km2) also 3; no state or UT touches more; every other border state touches 1 or 2
facts.column: Neighbouring countries whose land border the state touches (number)
facts.source: Ministry of Home Affairs, Annual Report 2024-25, Chapter 3 paras 3.9, 3.16, 3.22, 3.25, 3.26, 3.28 (state lists per border); area from ISFR 2023 Table 2.4
facts.stays_true: Fixed by the boundaries named; changes only with a new state or a boundary treaty.
facts.lead: Tied at 3 with West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh, so no sole-first claim; Sikkim is 12.5 times smaller than West Bengal and 11.8 times smaller than Arunachal.
facts.size_effect: The point of the fact is the small size; the count is of countries, not length.
facts.caution: The count is our own, from the Ministry's lists of states per border; the report prints no such count. Afghanistan (106 km) is not assigned to any state or UT by the report, so J&K and Ladakh are counted only for what the report names. 'Second-smallest state' is by ISFR Table 2.4 areas (Goa 3,702, Sikkim 7,096, Tripura 10,486).

facts.fact: In April 2025 Telangana (16) and Andhra Pradesh (13) had 29 of India's 83 specified dams under construction.
facts.measure: Specified dams under construction
facts.compare: India 83; Madhya Pradesh 10, Chhattisgarh 9. Two states hold 35% of the total.
facts.source: National Dam Safety Authority, Ministry of Jal Shakti: National Register of Specified Dams, April 2025 (summary table, page iv)
facts.stays_true: Does NOT stay true: dams under construction are completed over the next years. Valid only as 'April 2025'.
facts.lead: 3 over Andhra Pradesh (1.23x)
facts.size_effect: Not a size effect: the two states have 8.4% of India's area (Telangana 3.4%, Andhra Pradesh 5.0%) but 34.9% of dams under construction.
facts.caution: Weak for an evergreen bank: a construction count that will fall as dams finish. Telangana and Andhra Pradesh were one state until 2014; the register gives no reason for the concentration.

facts.fact: Punjab grows crops on 82% of its land (net sown area, 2023-24); India's average is 42%.
facts.measure: Net sown area as a share of geographical area
facts.source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Tables 54 and 56 (from Land Use Statistics at a Glance, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare); geographical area from Lok Sabha Q 304 (ISFR 2023)
facts.stays_true: Net sown area has moved by under two points in 20 years (Punjab 83.4% in 2004-05, 82.3% in 2013-14, 81.6% in 2023-24).
facts.lead: Haryana is 2.1 points behind: below the brief's lead test, so no rank claimed
facts.size_effect: A share of the state's own land.
facts.caution: Do not say 'most': Haryana is 80%. Provisional. Do not run on the same day as the Punjab irrigation fact.

facts.fact: Maharashtra has 39 registered agricultural GIs, such as Nashik Grapes and Alphonso mango, 14 more than any other State.
facts.measure: Registered Geographical Indications of kind Agricultural
facts.compare: Next: Tamil Nadu and Kerala with 25 each; 71% of Maharashtra's 55 GIs are agricultural against 33% across India
facts.source: GI Registry (DPIIT), Year-wise GI Application Register as on 31 March 2026 (ipindia.gov.in, file created 27 May 2026); previous edition: State-wise Registered GI list as on 31 Dec 2025
facts.stays_true: The register grows every year (125 rows in April 2025 to March 2026), so a State can be overtaken; true as stated for 31 March 2026. Next edition: the Registry's next year-wise register.
facts.lead: 14 ahead (56% more) than the next State; on the 31 Dec 2025 list (shared GIs counted under each State) it was 38 against 25 for Tamil Nadu, with Karnataka 24
facts.size_effect: Maharashtra is 9.3% of India's people but holds a 15% share of agricultural GIs and a 71% share within its own GIs; the lead over equally large States is wide.
facts.caution: Kind is the register's 'Goods' column: 'Agriculture' and 'Agricultural' merged; 'Food Stuff' is a separate kind. 39 counts Nagpur Orange once under Maharashtra and once under Madhya Pradesh (shared). Names in the example are from the register.

facts.fact: Delhi has 170 of India's 3,685 centrally protected monuments, 4.6% of them, on 0.05% of India's land.
facts.measure: Centrally protected monuments and sites (ASI)
facts.compare: 115 per 1,000 sq km against 1.1 for India and 14 in Puducherry, the next densest; Delhi area 1,483 sq km (Census 2011)
facts.source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 84, 1 Dec 2025, Annexure-I (ASI figures); cross-checked with ASI list PDF CPM_List.pdf (created 8 Apr 2025)
facts.stays_true: Changes by a few when the Government notifies or de-notifies a site (3 Delhi sites were removed in 2024-25); no fixed schedule, the next Parliament answer or ASI list shows it. Area is Census 2011 (fixed).
facts.lead: 8.0x the density of Puducherry
facts.size_effect: Opposite of a size effect: Delhi is among the smallest territories (Census 2011 area 1,483 sq km); its share of monuments is about 100 times its share of land (102x).
facts.caution: The count moves slightly: ASI's list PDF (April 2025) has Delhi 172 of 3,698, Parliament (1 Dec 2025) has 170 of 3,685 after delistings, ASI's web page says 3,679 in total. Use the December 2025 figures; the density lead over Puducherry is huge on every version. Monuments are counted without grouping by kind.

facts.fact: Rajasthan, India's largest state, has 17.9 railway route km per 1,000 sq km, below India's 21; Uttar Pradesh has 36.6 (March 2024).
facts.measure: Railway route km per 1,000 sq km of area
facts.compare: India 21.0; Uttar Pradesh 36.6 on 70% of Rajasthan's area. Rajasthan has 6,135 route km, 8.9% of India's, on 10.4% of its area.
facts.source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25, Table 145 (data of the Ministry of Railways), 11 Dec 2025
facts.stays_true: Route length changes slowly (a new line or a gauge change adds or removes a few km); the Handbook is annual (the 2025-26 edition will carry end-March 2025). Density ranks have held since 2020.
facts.lead: Rajasthan's 342,239 sq km is 11% more than Madhya Pradesh's, the second-largest
facts.size_effect: Rate per area, so size is divided out. In absolute length Rajasthan's 6,135 route km is the second longest network after Uttar Pradesh (8,823).
facts.caution: The Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 and Annual Statistical Statements 2024-25 give route length by zonal railway only, so the state split comes from the RBI Handbook, which prints the Ministry of Railways as its source. Area is ISFR 2023 geographical area (Forest Survey of India). Route km is the length of line open, not track km. Much of Rajasthan's area is desert with low population; do not imply the state is neglected: the source gives no cause.

facts.fact: Delhi's 1,483 sq km hold 3 of India's 45 World Heritage properties: Red Fort, Humayun's Tomb and Qutb Minar.

facts.size_effect: Opposite of a size effect: area 1,483 sq km (Census 2011).

facts.fact: Telangana has 60,858 cooperative societies, 7% of India's, with 3% of the people (National Cooperative Database, March 2026).

facts.fact: No single mother tongue was named by more than 12.3% of Nagaland's people in Census 2011; in Kerala, 97.0% named Malayalam.

facts.fact: Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat hold 4,591 of 6,628 specified dams, 69.3 per cent, on 24.7 per cent of land (April 2025).
facts.measure: Specified dams in three states
facts.compare: The other 26 states and UTs with dams hold 2,037. Three-state area share 24.7%, people share 20.5%.
facts.source: National Dam Safety Authority, Ministry of Jal Shakti: National Register of Specified Dams, April 2025 (summary table, page iv)
facts.stays_true: Counts change only when dams are completed or added to the register; the register is re-issued every few years (2023, then April 2025). The April 2025 figures stay true as dated. Next edition date not announced.
facts.lead: Third-placed Gujarat has 525, the fourth, Chhattisgarh, 322
facts.size_effect: Share of dams 69.3% against 24.7% of area.
facts.caution: Counts 'specified dams' under the Dam Safety Act 2021 (above 15 m, or 10-15 m with size conditions), compiled from state dam safety organisations; many are small tanks and earthen dams, not big-river dams. Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu have no entry. The 2023 register (6,138 completed dams) could not be fetched from the publisher, so the lead is checked against the 2025 edition only. Same table as built-01; use one or the other.

facts.fact: Sikkim's National Highways grew almost fivefold, from 149 km on 31 March 2014 to 730 km on 30 June 2025.
facts.measure: Length of National Highways
facts.compare: x4.90; next fastest Maharashtra x2.95, India x1.60. Sikkim now has 103 km of NH per 1,000 sq km against India's 44.5.
facts.source: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, reply to Lok Sabha Starred Question 75, 24 July 2025, Annexure-I
facts.stays_true: Both dates are fixed, so the statement stays true as dated. National Highway length keeps changing as roads are notified and built, so the 'now' position can change in the next Parliament answer.
facts.lead: x4.90 against x2.95 for the next, Maharashtra (66% faster)
facts.size_effect: A small base (149 km) makes the multiple large; the 2025 density (103 km per 1,000 sq km, area 7,096 sq km) is 2.3x India's. Do not claim Sikkim has the densest NHs: Nagaland (101) is within 3%.
facts.caution: National Highway length grows partly by notifying existing state roads as NHs: the same answer says about 54,004 km of state roads were notified as NHs since April 2014. Say 'length of notified National Highways', not 'new roads built'. The increase is 581 km: small in absolute terms.

facts.fact: Six north-eastern states, from Mizoram to Tripura, have forest cover on over 70% of their land; India's share is 21.8% (ISFR 2023).
facts.state: Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Manipur, Nagaland, Tripura
facts.measure: Forest cover as % of state area
facts.value: Mizoram 85.34; Arunachal Pradesh 78.67; Meghalaya 75.65; Manipur 74.28; Nagaland 73.72; Tripura 72.33
facts.compare: India 21.76%; lowest of the six, Tripura 72.33%, is 3.3 times India
facts.source: Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report 2023, Vol. 1, Table 2.4

facts.size_effect: Share of own area; the six range from 10,486 to 83,743 km2.
facts.caution: Threshold facts shift with every edition (check ISFR 2025). Same 'forest cover includes plantations' caution as land-01. Do not add Lakshadweep or A&N (UTs) to the count without saying so.

facts.fact: Puducherry has 1,830 MBBS seats, 106 for every lakh people, against 7.9 for India (2024-25).
facts.measure: MBBS seats per lakh population
facts.compare: India 7.9; next Andaman and Nicobar Islands 28.1, Telangana 22.1, Karnataka 18.0. Puducherry 9 colleges, projected population 1.72 million (1 Mar 2025).
facts.source: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (National Medical Commission data), reply to Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3054, 9 Aug 2024, Annexure

facts.lead: 3.8x the next (Andaman and Nicobar Islands, a UT); 4.8x Telangana, the next state
facts.size_effect: A rate per head. Small base: nine colleges.
facts.caution: Seats change every year (the source says: 'Data for 2024-25 may vary on granting of permission by NMC'). Later Lok Sabha answers give Puducherry 1,873 seats (Aug 2025). Many Puducherry seats are in private colleges and serve students from other states, so seats per resident overstate local supply: the source does not break this down; do not claim doctors per patient.

facts.fact: India's first three registered GIs, in 2004-05, were Darjeeling Tea (West Bengal), Pochampalli Ikat (Telangana) and Chanderi Sarees (Madhya Pradesh).

facts.size_effect: Chronology, not size.

facts.caution: Always say 'in Census 2011' and 'districts then'. The lgdirectory.gov.in count today could not be collected (CAPTCHA), so no 'today' version exists.

facts.fact: India's only mixed natural and cultural World Heritage property, Khangchendzonga National Park, is in Sikkim, a State of 7,096 sq km.
facts.measure: Mixed (natural and cultural) World Heritage properties
facts.compare: 1 of India's 45 properties; Sikkim is 0.22% of India's land and 0.05% of its people (Census 2011)
facts.source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, India page (Internet Archive capture 12 Oct 2026) and data.unesco.org dataset whc001; State from Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3591 of 11 Aug 2025, Annexure-I

facts.size_effect: Small State holding the only property of its kind; no size effect.

facts.source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 2237, 9 Dec 2024, Annexure
facts.stays_true: A closed ten-year period, true as stated; later years' surveys do not change it. A new ten-year table would only appear if Parliament is asked again.

facts.size_effect: Punjab is 1.5% of India's land, so the lead is not size.

facts.fact: Six present-day States and UTs date from 1 November 1956: Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Lakshadweep.

Several other States and UTs also date from 1956 or earlier but their dates are not footnoted. Use only if framed as 'reorganised on'.

facts.source: GI Registry (DPIIT), Year-wise GI Application Register as on 31 March 2026 (ipindia.gov.in, file created 27 May 2026); previous edition: State-wise Registered GI list as on 31 Dec 2025

facts.fact: One Rajya Sabha seat stands for 6.1 lakh people in Sikkim (Census 2011) and 68.5 lakh in Rajasthan.

facts.compare: India 5,196,802 (233 seats); Sikkim 610,577 (1 seat); Madhya Pradesh 6,602,437

facts.why: people per Rajya Sabha seat: the same debate.

facts.fact: By Census 2011, one Lok Sabha seat stood for 27.4 lakh people in Rajasthan and 6.1 lakh in Sikkim.

facts.as_on: Seats: 2024 general election (2008 delimitation); population 1 March 2011
facts.stays_true: Until the Lok Sabha seats are readjusted after the first census taken after 2026 (Constitution, Article 82 proviso); the Census 2011 figure itself does not change.

facts.caution: Politically sensitive: state it as arithmetic with 'Census 2011' and nothing about fairness or cause. Seat numbers are set on the 1971 census (Article 81(3) proviso), a rule the Constitution states; the source does not link it to this gap, so do not claim a cause. Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are left out (2011 boundaries differ).
facts.why: people per Lok Sabha seat: arithmetic, but it is the delimitation debate. The channel's rule is no politics.

facts.fact: Haryana and Chandigarh both date from 1 November 1966, the day the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 took effect.
facts.measure: Appointed day of the Punjab Reorganisation Act 1966 (Act 31 of 1966)
facts.compare: Chandigarh 1 November 1966; Punjab and Himachal Pradesh's boundaries changed the same day
facts.source: The Constitution of India as on 1 May 2024, First Schedule entries 16 (Haryana) and II-7 (Chandigarh) and footnotes, Ministry of Law and Justice, Legislative Department
facts.stays_true: A date in law; does not change.
facts.lead: n/a (dates)
facts.size_effect: A date.
facts.caution: Haryana's entry was amended on 15 September 1983 (Haryana and Uttar Pradesh Alteration of Boundaries Act 1979) but the State dates from 1966.

facts.fact: Ladakh has 11 registered GIs, 9 of them handicrafts, and 7 of the 11 were registered between April 2025 and March 2026.
facts.measure: Registered Geographical Indications
facts.compare: On 31 Dec 2025 Ladakh had 4; projected population about 0.30 million (1 March 2026)
facts.source: GI Registry (DPIIT), Year-wise GI Application Register as on 31 March 2026 (ipindia.gov.in, file created 27 May 2026); previous edition: State-wise Registered GI list as on 31 Dec 2025
facts.stays_true: Date-bound: 11 as of 31 March 2026; further registrations will raise it. Next edition: next year-wise register.
facts.lead: No rank claim
facts.size_effect: A small-population UT; no size effect.
facts.caution: Weak as evergreen: the count rose from 4 to 11 in one quarter. Use only as 'as of March 2026'. The register prints Ladakh Likir Pottery under Assam, so Ladakh could be 12.

facts.fact: Sikkim became a State of the Indian Union on 26 April 1975, through the Constitution's Thirty-sixth Amendment.
facts.measure: Effective date of the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act 1975, s.2 and s.4
facts.compare: Sikkim has 1 Lok Sabha seat and 1 Rajya Sabha seat; population 6.1 lakh (Census 2011)
facts.source: The Constitution of India as on 1 May 2024, First Schedule entry 21 and footnote 3, Fourth Schedule footnote 5, Ministry of Law and Justice, Legislative Department
facts.stays_true: A date in law; does not change.
facts.lead: n/a (dates)
facts.size_effect: A date.
facts.caution: Use the Schedule's wording ('the territories comprised in Sikkim' were added by the Amendment); do not add a history the source does not give.

facts.fact: The Constitution fixes each State's Lok Sabha seats on the 1971 census until figures of the first census after 2026 are published.
facts.measure: Lok Sabha seats whose allotment to States rests on the 1971 census (Article 81(3) proviso)
facts.compare: Boundaries of constituencies inside each State follow the 2001 census (clause (3)(ii)); the Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats, Atlas 2024 (ECI) notes the last delimitation was under the Delimitation Act 2002 on Census 2001
facts.source: The Constitution of India as on 1 May 2024, Ministry of Law and Justice, Legislative Department, Article 81(3) proviso and Article 82 provisos (PDF pages 68-69)
facts.stays_true: Until the relevant figures of the first census taken after 2026 are published (results of the census due from 2027) and Parliament readjusts the seats. Check for any later amendment before use.
facts.lead: n/a
facts.size_effect: A rule in the Constitution, not a count.
facts.caution: Politically live topic. Quote the text only: no view on delimitation. The constituency boundaries inside a State use the 2001 census (clause (3)(ii)). The text was read in the 1 May 2024 edition; confirm no amendment since.
facts.why: the 1971-census freeze on Lok Sabha seats: the Constitution's words, but it is the delimitation debate.
